info.title: Nodium API
info.description:
Nodium connects your backend to WhatsApp (the official Cloud API). Nodium carries; your software decides.

This API gives your software everything it needs: connect numbers, send and receive messages, manage templates and broadcasts, subscribe to signed webhooks — and create and manage your own customers (tenants).

One key belongs to your account. Every call acts on one client: the one the key is pinned to, otherwise the one named by the `Nodium-Tenant` header, otherwise your own company. Nothing crosses over.

Every success is `{ "data": … }`; every refusal is `{ "error": { "status", "code", "message", "detail", "param", "doc_url", "requestId" } }`. Test `error.code`, never the text.

Conversation.description: A conversation: one contact on one WhatsApp number — the 24-hour window and the delivery receipts.

identity.description: Their phone number, or their WhatsApp user id when the number is hidden.

blocked.description: Blocked contacts are kept out of the inbox.

open.description: Whether free text can be sent now. Always `true` when the rule does not apply.

minutesLeft.description: Minutes left, `0` when closed, `null` when the rule does not apply.

lastInboundAt.description: When the contact last wrote, ISO 8601. This opens the 24-hour window.

direction.description: From the contact, or to them.

sender.description: Who speaks: the contact, your software (`api`, through a key), a person in the console (`user`), or Nodium (`system`).

senderName.description: The person's name, or your key's label.

apiKeyId.description: The key that sent it, when it went through the API.

textContent.description: Its text. For a template, the rendered text.

mediaUrl.description: Where to download its file (`GET /messages/{id}/media`), or `null`.

status.description: Delivery status. `queued`: waiting to leave (`queue: true`).

providerMessageId.description: The id at the messaging provider (WhatsApp `wamid`), or `null`.

error.description: Why it failed, as the provider said, or `null`.

errorInfo.description: The failure explained, when `status` is `failed` and the provider gave a code; otherwise `null`. A send can answer HTTP 200 or 201 with `status: "failed"`: test `status`, then read this.

code.description: The provider's error code (Meta's, for example `131047`).

action.description: What to do about it. When `actor` is `client`, written to be passed on to your client as is.

actor.description: Who acts: `you` (your code or console), `client` (the owner of the number), `nodium`, or `wait` (the refusal is temporary: nobody needs to act).

form.description: The buttons or list sent with it, or `null`.

reply.description: For a tapped button or chosen list row: `{ id, title }`. Otherwise `null`.

location.description: A location the contact sent: `{ latitude, longitude, name, address }`, or `null`.

origin.description: `phone` when the message was written from the WhatsApp Business app of a coexistence number, otherwise `null`.

imported.description: True for a message taken from the phone's chat history (coexistence), not received live.

conversationId.description: The conversation the message belongs to — opened by this call, or reused.

duplicate.description: `true` when this `idempotencyKey` was already used: the message returned is the first one, nothing was sent again.

phone.description: Their phone number, E.164 digits, or `null`.

externalId.description: Your own id for them, or `null`.

optInAt.description: When they agreed to receive messages, or `null`.

optOutAt.description: When they withdrew — on WhatsApp by tapping "Stop" — or `null`. It overrides `optInAt`.

Channel.description: A WhatsApp number the workspace speaks from.

id.description: The channel id — the `channelId` you send from.

identity.description: Its public identity: the business phone number id.

isActive.description: An inactive channel neither sends nor receives.

isTest.description: A test channel: the sandbox (the shared Nodium number) or the demo channel.

paymentMissing.description: Meta refused a paid message because the client's WhatsApp account has no payment method (error 131042). The client adds one in WhatsApp Manager; it clears once a template is delivered.

id.description: The template id — the `templateId` you send.

category.description: Meta's category. Marketing ones are refused to contacts who opted out.

status.description: Where it stands at Meta, across its client's WhatsApp accounts. Only `approved` can be sent. `failed`: the deposit at Meta did not happen; deploy again.

deployedAt.description: When it was first deployed, ISO 8601; `null` for a draft.

headerMedia.description: Its image, video or document header: `kind`, `sampleId`, `mimeType`, `filename`, `size`. `null` for a text header or none.

authentication.description: For an `AUTHENTICATION` template: `securityRecommendation` and `codeExpirationMinutes` (`null` = no expiry line). `null` for any other category.

body.description: Its text, with `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`… placeholders. For an `AUTHENTICATION` template, a readable copy of the text Meta writes.

WebhookSubscription.description: An address Nodium calls, and for which events.

channelIds.description: The channels (numbers) whose events are delivered; empty means all channels.

lastDeliveredAt.description: The last successful call, ISO 8601, or `null`.

lastError.description: What went wrong last time, or `null`.

previousSecretValidUntil.description: During a rotation: until when the old secret still signs. `null` otherwise.

WebhookDelivery.description: One event delivered — or to deliver — to one subscription.

id.description: The delivery id, also sent as `X-Nodium-Delivery`.

eventId.description: The event's own id (`evt_…`), the same across redeliveries: deduplicate on it.

responseStatus.description: The HTTP status your server answered, or `null`.

nextAttemptAt.description: When the next attempt is due, for a pending delivery.

ApiRequest.description: One call made with an API key.

clientId.description: The client the call acted on, or `null` for an account-level call (`/tenants`, `/keys`).

path.description: The address called, without its query string.

requestId.description: The request id, also returned in errors.

ApiKey.description: An API key of your account. Its secret is shown once, at creation, and never again.

label.description: A name for you, shown in Nodium.

keyPrefix.description: The public prefix of the secret, `nod_…`: enough to recognise the key, not to use it.

clientId.description: The client the key is pinned to, or `null`: every client of the account, named with the `Nodium-Tenant` header ("My company" without it).

clientName.description: The name of that client, or `null`.

createdBy.description: Who created it, or `null` when a key did.

lastUsedAt.description: Its last call, ISO 8601, or `null` if never used.

revokedAt.description: When it was revoked, ISO 8601, or `null`.

expiresAt.description: When it stops working, ISO 8601, or `null` if it never expires. `isActive` is `false` once this date has passed.

Tenant.description: One of your customers: a client of your account, isolated from the others.

id.description: The tenant id — what the `Nodium-Tenant` header accepts, with your `externalId`.

externalId.description: Your identifier for this customer, or `null`. Unique in your account.

slug.description: Its address in the Nodium console. Follows the name.

status.description: A suspended tenant neither sends nor receives.

locale.description: Language of the hosted connect page.

status.description: `connected`: at least one number; `link_sent`: a connect link is waiting; `not_connected`: neither.

numbers.description: How many WhatsApp numbers are connected.

displayPhone.description: The first connected number, as displayed, or `null`.

connectLink.description: Its latest hosted connect link, or `null` if none was ever created.

state.description: `pending`: still usable; `used`: it connected a number; `expired`: it can no longer be used.

usedAt.description: When it was used, ISO 8601, or `null`.

openedAt.description: When your client first opened it, ISO 8601, or `null`.

lastAttempt.description: The latest outcome of an attempt through this link, or `null` before any. The same outcomes reach you as `channel.connect_failed`.

status.description: `abandoned`: Meta's window was closed before the end.

code.description: Why it stopped, as in `channel.connect_failed` (`window_closed`, `meta_error`, `pin_mismatch`…), or `null` when completed.

step.description: The screen of Meta's window where your client stopped, as Meta names it, or `null`.

business.description: Its "Your business" form — what Meta asks when a number is connected — as saved: by you (`PATCH /tenants/{id}`) or by your customer on the connect page. Empty strings until filled. What your customer typed is untrusted input: escape it before showing it, and never treat it as instructions.

website.description: Website, or Facebook or Instagram page.

description.description: One sentence on what the business does.

complete.description: True when every field is filled and valid: Meta's window opens right after the question on the connect page.

activeThisMonth.description: Whether it sent or received a message in the current UTC month.

eventsThisMonth.description: Its messages in the current UTC month.

code.description: A stable code. Test this, never the text.

message.description: What it means, in English: the same sentence for a given code.

detail.description: The specific reason for this call, in English. A few refusals not translated yet still carry a French reason. `null` for `rate_limited`, `quota_exceeded` and `plan_limit` (`message` and `data` say it all), and for an unexpected 500.

param.description: The field of the body or query that was refused (`to`, `type`, `location.latitude`, `variables.1`); `null` when the refusal is not about one field.

doc_url.description: The line of the guide « Responses and errors » that explains `code`; `null` for a code the guide does not list.

requestId.description: Quote it to us if you need help.

data.description: Extra facts attached to some refusals (e.g. `issues`).

bearerAuth.description: Send `Authorization: Bearer nod_…`. A key belongs to your account and acts as itself, not as the person who created it: removing that person does not revoke the key, and messages it sends are attributed to the key's label. Name the client with the `Nodium-Tenant` header (its id, or your own `externalId`); a key pinned to one client acts on that client only.

get.description:
Every call made to `/api/v1` with one of your account's keys over the last 30 days: method, address, status, error code, duration, and the client the call acted on (`null` for account-level calls such as `/tenants` or `/keys`). Newest first. Use it to see why a call failed without asking us.

A key that is not pinned sees every call and may narrow them with `clientId` (or the `Nodium-Tenant` header); a key pinned to a client sees only the calls made on that client. Neither bodies, headers nor query strings are kept. A call refused because the key itself was wrong is not listed: we cannot tell whose it was.

200.description: A page of calls, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` for the next page; `null` at the end.

401.description: Missing, malformed or revoked API key.

404.description: Not found, or outside your account.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded — 600 calls per minute per client (per key when pinned), 6,000 per key.

post.description:
Creates another key for your account — for key rotation, or to give a separate system its own key. Without `clientId`, the key acts on every client of the account; with it, the key is pinned to that client: it acts there without the `Nodium-Tenant` header, and naming another client answers 404.

The response carries the secret **once and never again**: store it now.

delete.description:
Revokes a key of your account at once: its next call is refused. The key stays listed, revoked, as a trace.

A key revoking **itself** must say so with `?confirmSelf=true` — otherwise the call answers `409 own_key`, so that a rotation script that picks the wrong id does not lock itself out.

get.summary: See what this month will cost
get.description:
Returns this month's bill so far for your account: your plan, the WhatsApp numbers connected against those included, the messages included and used, the media storage used, and the estimated total.

A **connected number** is an active, non-test WhatsApp number of any of your clients. Messages are counted across the account: every message received or sent, templates included, test channels excluded. Beyond the allowance, a plan either bills each started block of `eventsPerOverageUnit` messages, up to the overage cap you set (`capCents`), or blocks sends until the month ends (`blocking`, error `quota_exceeded`).

The total is an estimate before tax; the invoice is the reference. Meta's messaging fees are never included: your clients pay them to Meta directly.

200.description: This month's plan, numbers, messages, media and estimated total.

plan.description: Your plan: `key`, `name`, `nameEn`. `null` when no plan applies.

numbers.description: Connected numbers: `connected`, `included` (`null` = no limit), `extra` (billed), `priceCents` (per extra number per month).

messages.description: Messages: `allowance` (`null` = no quota), `used`, `overageUnits` (billed blocks), `overagePriceCents`, `eventsPerOverageUnit`, `blocking`, `capCents` (your overage cap), `ceiling` (where sends stop).

media.description: Media storage: `usedMb`, `includedMb` (`null` = no quota), `extraGb` (billed), `priceCents` (per extra GB per month).

basePriceCents.description: The fixed monthly price, in cents. `null` for a custom plan.

estimatedTotalCents.description: The estimated total so far, in cents, before tax.

periodEnd.description: When the month ends (UTC, ISO 8601): the allowance resets and the invoice is issued.

post.description:
Sends an approved WhatsApp template to a group: a list of contacts, or every contact who opted in. Everything is checked first; recipients then leave in batches, and `counts.sent` grows as they do — follow it with `GET /broadcasts/{id}`. **Consent is honoured**: a contact without opt-in, opted out or blocked receives nothing, and is counted. Try the target first with `POST /broadcasts/preview`. Recipients are taken in turn across the broadcasts being sent, so a large one does not hold the others back. The number's messaging tier is honoured: a broadcast that reaches more recipients than the tier allows per 24 hours is refused, and a smaller one pauses by itself when the day's allowance is used, then continues. If sends are refused over and over for an account reason (payment, quality, rate limit, token, plan allowance), the broadcast is paused: `status` is `paused` with its reason, and `POST /broadcasts/{id}/resume` continues it.

**Later, or step by step.** With `scheduledAt` the broadcast waits (`status: scheduled`) and leaves at that time. With `draft: true` nothing leaves (`status: draft`): add recipients with `POST /broadcasts/{id}/recipients`, then start it with `POST /broadcasts/{id}/send`. The target is resolved when recipients are written: a contact who opts in afterwards is not added.

200.description: The broadcast id and its starting counts.

status.description: `sending`, `scheduled` or `draft`; `finished` when no one can receive it.

401.description: Missing, malformed or revoked API key.

404.description: Not found, or outside your account.

409.description: `template_not_approved` — The template is not approved by Meta at this client yet.

422.description:
`scheduled_at_invalid` — `scheduledAt` is not a valid ISO 8601 date, or is less than a minute ahead.

`broadcast_exceeds_messaging_limit` — The broadcast reaches more recipients than the number's messaging tier allows per 24 hours; `data.limit`, `data.recipients` and `data.tier` say how many. Send it in smaller broadcasts, or wait for a higher tier.

name.description: A name for you, up to 120 characters.

contactIds.description: The contacts to reach, up to 10,000. Or use `allOptIn`.

allOptIn.description: `true` to reach every contact who opted in.

channelId.description: The number to send from. Optional when the client has a single active number.

variables.description: The values of the placeholders, the same for everyone: `{ "1": "value" }`.

scheduledAt.description: When to send, ISO 8601, at least a minute ahead. Leave it out to send now.

draft.description: `true` writes the broadcast without sending it. The target is optional then.

get.description: One broadcast and its counts. `draft` waits for `POST /broadcasts/{id}/send`; `scheduled` leaves at `sendAt`. Recipients leave in batches, so poll this route to follow `counts.sent` and `counts.failed` until `status` is `finished` (or `cancelled`). A recipient counts as `sent` once WhatsApp has accepted its message, and as `failed` once the message is refused for good: a message waiting for a new attempt is in neither count yet. `paused` means sends were refused over and over for an account reason: `pauseReason` says why (`pauseInfo` explains a Meta refusal), and `POST /broadcasts/{id}/resume` continues it.

pausedAt.description: When the broadcast was paused, or `null` when it is not paused.

pauseReason.description: The refusal that paused it, or `null`.

pauseInfo.description: When the reason carries a Meta code: `code`, `title`, `action` and `actor` explaining it; otherwise `null`.

sendAt.description: When it starts or started; `null` for a draft.

sentAt.description: When the last recipient was handled, or `null` while sending.

request.description: The body of `POST /broadcasts` that would send it again: same template, number, values and target. A target listing more than 200 contacts is left out (`contactIds` absent).

get.description:
Every event Nodium emits — the ones your webhooks receive — is also written to a numbered log, kept 30 days. Read it from a cursor instead of depending on webhook deliveries: the webhook is a doorbell, the log is the truth. Each entry is the webhook envelope (`id`, `event`, `workspace_id`, `external_id`, `occurred_at`, `data`) plus its `seq`.

Start without `after`: `data` is empty and `next_after` is the current head — store it as your first cursor. Then call with `after` set to the last `next_after` you kept, and repeat while `next_after` moves: a page may be empty and still move forward (events of other clients are skipped). When a call returns the same `next_after` you sent, you are up to date; come back when a webhook rings, or every minute. Keep `next_after` only after you have stored the page.

Entries come in `seq` order and none is skipped: an entry is returned only once every earlier one is settled, so a recent entry can appear a moment after the webhook that announced it. Deduplicate on `id` (a webhook delivery and the log carry the same one). `seq` is unique across the whole log, not per client: expect gaps.

A key that sees every client of the account reads all of them, unless the `Nodium-Tenant` header names one; a key pinned to one client reads that client only. Entries older than your plan's content retention keep their envelope but an empty `data`.

200.description: A page of events and the cursor to continue from.

data.description: A page of the event log.

post.description:
Sends a message from one of your WhatsApp numbers to one person. You name the number (`channelId`) and the person (`to`, or `recipient`); Nodium finds their conversation, or opens it, and sends. Everything goes through this one call, chosen by `type`: free `text`, an `interactive` form (quick-reply buttons, a list, a location request, a WhatsApp Flow), a `location` pin, a contact card (`contacts`), an approved `template`, a file (`image`, `video`, `audio`, `document`), or a `reaction`. Fields that do not belong to the `type` are refused.

**The person.** `to` is a phone number in international format (E.164, for example `+33612345678`). A contact who does not expose a number is written to by `recipient`, their WhatsApp user id (`wa:FR.13491208655302741918`, as found in `GET /contacts`). Give one of the two, not both. Someone Nodium has never seen becomes a contact and gets a conversation on the spot.

**The 24-hour window is enforced here.** On WhatsApp you may only send free-form messages (every `type` except `template` and `reaction`) within 24 hours of the person's last message. Outside it, and to anyone who has never written to you, you get `window_closed` (409) and must send a `template` instead. Interactive forms count as free text for Meta.

**Files.** Upload the file first with `POST /media`, which returns a `mediaId` valid for 7 days, then send it here with `type` set to its kind. The same `mediaId` can be sent to many people.

**Idempotency.** An idempotency key is required on every call: the `idempotencyKey` field, or the `Idempotency-Key` request header (same value rules: 8 to 200 characters). Give it in one place, or in both with the same value; two different values are refused with `422 invalid_request`. Sending twice with the same key sends once and returns the first message with `duplicate: true`, even if the window has closed since. A retry must carry the same request (number, recipient, type and content): the same key with a different content is refused with `409 idempotency_key_conflict` and nothing is sent. `queue` and `scheduledAt` are not part of that comparison. A message written before this check existed is returned as a duplicate without being compared.

**Rate limit.** Free-form messages are limited to 600 per minute per key and per client (`429` with `Retry-After`); templates are not, they are governed by your plan's allowance.

The message is attributed to your key: the conversation shows the key's label, never a person who did nothing. With `queue: true` the call returns at once with the message `queued` (HTTP 202) and it leaves within a minute; follow it with the `message.sent` / `message.failed` webhooks. With `scheduledAt` the message is stored now with status `scheduled` (HTTP 202) and sent at that time instead; `queue` wins if you set both. A `reaction` is neither stored as a message nor queued: `message` is `null` in the answer.

**A refused send is not an HTTP error.** When the provider refuses the message, the call still answers 200 or 201 with `message.status: "failed"`, `message.error` (the provider's reason) and `message.errorInfo` (what happened, what to do, who acts). Always test `message.status`, not only the HTTP code. The `message.failed` webhook carries the same.

200.description: The message as stored, with its delivery status, and the id of the conversation it belongs to — new or reused.

401.description: Missing, malformed or revoked API key.

402.description: `quota_exceeded` — Your plan's monthly allowance is used up; `data.resetsAt` says when sends resume.

404.description:
`unknown_channel` — `channelId` is not one of this client's numbers.

`media_not_found` — `mediaId` is unknown, belongs to another client, or has expired (7 days): upload the file again.

`message_not_found` — The message to react to, or to quote, is not in this person's conversation.

409.description:
`channel_inactive` — This number is switched off: switch it on before sending from it.

`window_closed` — More than 24 hours since the person last wrote, or they never did. Send an approved `template` instead.

`contact_blocked` — This contact is blocked: nothing is sent to them.

`consent_missing` — A marketing template to a contact who opted out.

`template_not_approved` — The template is not approved by Meta at this client yet; `data.status` says where it stands there (`not_deployed`, `submitted`, `rejected`…).

`idempotency_key_conflict` — That key already served a request with different content (number, recipient, type, text, template values…). Retry with the exact same request, or use a new key; nothing is sent.

422.description:
`invalid_type` — `type` is missing or not one of the listed values.

`invalid_field` — A field was given that does not belong to this `type`.

`recipient_required` — Neither `to` nor `recipient` was given.

`recipient_invalid` — `to` is not a number in international format, `recipient` is not a `wa:…` id, or both were given.

`no_recipient` — This contact has no address to write to: neither a phone number nor a WhatsApp user id (`wa:…`).

`text_too_long` — The text is over 4,096 characters, the WhatsApp limit. Nothing is stored; `limit` says the maximum.

`caption_too_long` — The caption is over 1,024 characters, the WhatsApp limit.

`caption_unsupported` — WhatsApp shows no caption under audio — send the text separately.

`media_type_mismatch` — The file behind `mediaId` is not of the kind named by `type`.

`idempotency_key_required` — The idempotency key (`idempotencyKey` field or `Idempotency-Key` header) is missing or outside 8-200 characters.

`invalid_request` — Among others: the `Idempotency-Key` header and the `idempotencyKey` field are both given and differ; `detail` says which.

`invalid_form` — The form breaks a WhatsApp limit; `detail` says which.

`invalid_location` — The location is missing or its coordinates are out of range.

`invalid_contacts` — The contact cards are missing, empty, or over the limit of 1.

`template_holes_unfilled` — A placeholder has no value; `data.issues` lists them.

`template_header_invalid` — `headerMediaId` was given for a template without a media header, or the template's header sample is missing.

`template_buttons_invalid` — A button value does not match the template's buttons; `detail` says which.

`scheduled_at_invalid` — `scheduledAt` is not a valid ISO date, or is less than a minute away.

`queue_not_supported` — A reaction cannot be quoted, queued or scheduled.

429.description: `rate_limited` — More than 30 free-form messages in a minute for this key and client; wait `Retry-After` seconds.
